# Harmony Biosciences Announces Planned CEO Transition to Support Next Phase of Growth

Oct. 12, 2026, 07:00 AM

The Board of Directors has appointed Peter Anastasiou, former Harmony board member and current Sr. EVP and COO, to become President, Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board, effective January 1, 2027.

Current CEO Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire at the end of the year following a nine-year tenure at the Company, including as Chief Medical Officer, and step down as a member of the Board.

The Company reiterates full-year 2026 WAKIX® net revenue guidance of $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion, remains on track to report data from the multiple ascending dose (MAD) study of BP-205 in Q4 2026, and is focused on executing its previously communicated strategic priorities.

PLYMOUTH MEETING, Pa., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: HRMY) (“Harmony” or the “Company”) today announced that, as part of the Board of Directors’ succession planning, Peter Anastasiou, former Harmony board member and current Sr. EVP and Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed President, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board of Directors, effective January 1, 2027. He succeeds Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., who will retire as President and CEO and step down from the Board of Directors on December 31, 2026. To support the leadership transition, Dr. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor to the Company throughout 2027 to support Harmony’s growth objectives.

The planned succession comes as Harmony enters its next phase of growth from a position of financial and operational strength. The Company remains focused on its strategic priorities: growing the pitolisant franchise; advancing its diversified CNS pipeline, led by potential best-in-class orexin agonist BP-205; deploying capital strategically by transacting on value-creating assets; and protecting WAKIX® exclusivity. 

“Jeff has led Harmony through a period of strong growth, establishing WAKIX as a leading treatment in narcolepsy, advancing the pitolisant lifecycle management strategy, diversifying the pipeline for sustained long-term growth and leaving the Company in a position of financial strength,” said Jeffrey S. Aronin, founder and Chairman of the Board of Harmony. “The Board is grateful for Jeff’s leadership and his commitment to patients, employees and shareholders.”

“Peter is the right leader for Harmony’s next phase of growth. He has a deep understanding of our business and has been an important contributor to our strategy, pipeline and business development efforts,” continued Aronin. “Peter also brings more than three decades of biopharmaceutical experience, leading organizations in commercializing, acquiring and developing treatments for both broad and rare CNS diseases to serve patients and create value for shareholders.”

“It has been a privilege to lead Harmony through a phase of significant growth, and I am grateful to the Board for the opportunity to have served as CEO. It has also been my honor to work alongside such a talented team of individuals who are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients with unmet needs,” said Dayno. “Peter knows Harmony’s business exceptionally well, I have great confidence in his leadership, and I look forward to supporting him, the Board and the Company through this transition.”

“I am honored to serve as Harmony’s next CEO and am grateful to the Board for this opportunity. ## Meet Our Senior Leadership

Our company is led by a passionate team of professionals with deep experience in the pharmaceutical industry and a proven track record of success in developing and commercializing novel treatments for patients.

 Jeffrey M. Dayno, MD President and Chief Executive Officer 

 Jeffrey M. Dayno, MD 

 President and Chief Executive Officer 

Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., is President and Chief Executive Officer of Harmony Biosciences. A nationally recognized expert in neuroscience and leader at Harmony Biosciences since the company’s inception, Dr. Dayno is responsible for overseeing the company’s business growth, including Harmony’s successful completion of two acquisitions, two licensing deals, and buildout of the company’s clinical development pipeline. He has been the driving force behind Harmony’s patient-focused drug development model, which uses patient insights to inform clinical research programs and building a pipeline focused on potential, next-generation, innovative treatments to help people living with rare neurological diseases and unmet medical needs.

Dr. Dayno is a neurologist with 10 years of experience in clinical and academic medicine followed by over 25 years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry, touching every aspect of the business. He has held leadership roles at Merck & Co., Cephalon, and ViroPharma, building and leading clinical, regulatory, and medical affairs teams toward multiple NDA approvals and medical support for successful product launches. He also served as Principal Investigator on numerous clinical trials and has published and lectured extensively on various topics around evolving pharma business models, value creation and impact, as well as on numerous topics within the field of neurology.

Dr. Dayno is a 2026 EY Entrepreneur of the Year Greater Philadelphia Award winner and in 2023, was named to the PharmaVoice 100 list. In 2024, he received the Frank Baldino Bioscience CEO of the Year Award from Life Sciences Pennsylvania, which recognizes visionary leadership and active participation to advance the life sciences industry.

Dr. Dayno earned his medical degree from Temple University School of Medicine, completed his residency training in Neurology at Temple University Hospital, and completed a fellowship in Stroke and Cerebrovascular Disorders in the Department of Neurology at Henry Ford Hospital, which held a National Institutes of Health program grant in stroke research. He is on the Board of Life Sciences Pennsylvania (LSPA), serves on the Board of Managers for Life Science Cares Philadelphia, and is a member of the Board of Visitors of the Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University. Dr. Dayno has served as the Industry Representative for FDA’s Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee, as well as served as an expert on several FDA industry advisory panels.

Harmony Biosciences CEO Jeffrey Dayno to Retire December 31, 2026 - The Pharma Vanguard

# Harmony Biosciences CEO Jeffrey Dayno to Retire December 31, 2026

October 14, 2026

By Jon Napitupulu

 

Harmony Biosciences has a leadership gap opening at the top: Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., the company’s President, CEO, and board director, will retire effective December 31, 2026, leaving a narcolepsy-focused company with $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion in projected 2026 WAKIX revenue in need of a permanent chief executive heading into what looks like a critical commercial year.

Dayno will stay on as a non-executive advisor through 2027 to smooth the handoff, but the timing deserves scrutiny. WAKIX net revenue guidance sits at a billion-dollar threshold that the company has worked years to reach, and the stock was already trading well below even the low end of analyst price targets when the October 12 filing dropped. A CEO transition at that inflection point raises real questions about whether the exit is entirely planned or whether board-level pressure played a role, though the filing does not say either way.

Harmony’s entire commercial story runs through WAKIX (pitolisant), which earned FDA approval for excessive daytime sleepiness in adult narcolepsy patients in 2019 and built a market position in a space where oxybate formulations from Jazz Pharmaceuticals also compete. Whoever steps into the CEO seat inherits both the revenue momentum and the competitive pressure, with no diversified pipeline to absorb a stumble. Peter Anastasiou, currently Senior Executive Vice President, was named in the announcement materials as part of the transition context, per the company’s public disclosure, though the 8-K stops short of naming a permanent successor.

The name that fills the permanent CEO slot will tell investors whether Harmony is building toward a broader CNS platform or positioning the company for a sale while WAKIX revenue is at its peak.

Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 13, 2026, reporting that President and Chief Executive Officer Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire effective December 31, 2026, and that Chief Operating Officer Peter Anastasiou has been appointed to succeed him as President and CEO beginning January 1, 2027.

### Key Highlights

- CEO retirement: Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., will retire as President and CEO and step down as a Class I director, effective December 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.
- Successor named: Peter Anastasiou, the Company's current Chief Operating Officer, will become President and CEO effective January 1, 2027, at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time.
- Board appointment: The Board also appointed Mr. Anastasiou as a Class I director effective January 1, 2027, with a term expiring at the Company's 2027 Annual Meeting of Stockholders.
- Advisory role: Dr. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor to the Company through 2027.
- Prior experience: Mr. Anastasiou, age 55, has served as the Company's Chief Operating Officer since April 2026, and previously served as CEO of Capsida Biotherapeutics from January 2022 to October 2025.
- No additional director compensation: According to the filing, Mr. Anastasiou will not receive any additional compensation for his service as a director.

## Leadership Transition Details at Harmony Biosciences

According to the filing, the leadership change is described as part of "a leadership succession plan." Dr. Dayno's retirement as President, CEO, and Class I director takes effect December 31, 2026, after which he will transition to a non-executive advisory role through 2027. The Company, traded on NASDAQ:HRMY, made the announcement on October 12, 2026.

The filing states that the Board appointed Peter Anastasiou, currently serving as Chief Operating Officer, to fill the CEO role starting January 1, 2027. Mr. Anastasiou, age 55, joined the Company as Chief Operating Officer in April 2026. Before that, he served as CEO and board member of Capsida Biotherapeutics from January 2022 to October 2025. From November 2009 to December 2021, according to the filing, he held multiple roles at Lundbeck, including Executive Vice President and President of North America and Chief Commercial Officer for the U.S. The filing notes that Lundbeck is "a pharmaceutical company publicly traded on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange."

The filing further discloses that Mr. Anastasiou previously served as a member of the Company's Board from November 2023 to April 2026. He holds a B.A. in Economics and Management from Albion College and an M.B.A. from the Kelley School of Business, Indiana University. The filing states there are no arrangements or understandings between Mr. Anastasiou and any other person regarding his selection, no family relationships with any director or executive officer, and no transactions requiring disclosure under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.

## What Was Disclosed

The 8-K disclosed a CEO succession plan at Harmony Biosciences: Jeffrey Dayno will retire on December 31, 2026, and Peter Anastasiou, current COO, will assume the President and CEO role and a Class I board seat on January 1, 2027.

Harmony Biosciences names Peter Anastasiou CEO effective Jan 1, 2027, reaffirms 2026 WAKIX guidance – Minichart

Posted on October 13, 2026 at 8:44 pm (GMT+8)

 

Harmony Biosciences Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: HRMY) announced that Peter Anastasiou, currently Senior EVP and Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed President, Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board, effective January 1, 2027. He succeeds Jeffrey M. Dayno, M.D., who will retire as President and CEO and step down from the Board on December 31, 2026, ending a nine-year tenure that included serving as Chief Medical Officer. Dr. Dayno will serve as a non-executive advisor through 2027 to support the transition.

The planned succession comes as the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 WAKIX net revenue guidance of $1.0 billion to $1.04 billion and said it remains on track to report data from the multiple ascending dose (MAD) study of BP-205 in the fourth quarter of 2026. Harmony also stated it does not expect any change in the timing of key commercial and pipeline milestones, and remains focused on its strategic priorities: growing the pitolisant franchise, advancing its CNS pipeline led by BP-205, deploying capital strategically through value-creating transactions, and protecting WAKIX exclusivity.

## Leadership Transition Details

Anastasiou has served as Senior EVP and COO and previously spent three years on Harmony’s Board of Directors. Before joining Harmony, he was CEO and a board member of Capsida Biotherapeutics for nearly four years, where he raised more than $165 million in capital and secured partnerships with AbbVie and Lilly. Earlier, at Lundbeck, he served as Executive Vice President, member of the global executive committee, and President of North America, leading approximately 1,200 employees, delivering annual net revenues exceeding $1.5 billion, and achieving profit margins greater than 60%. He also held management roles at Neurocrine, Bristol-Myers Squibb and Lilly, and holds an M.B.A. from Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business.

“Peter is the right leader for Harmony’s next phase of growth. He has a deep understanding of our business and has been an important contributor to our strategy, pipeline and business development efforts,” said Jeffrey S. Aronin, founder and Chairman of the Board. “Peter also brings more than three decades of biopharmaceutical experience, leading organizations in commercializing, acquiring and developing treatments for both broad and rare CNS diseases to serve patients and create value for shareholders.”

## Why It Matters to Shareholders

An orderly CEO succession plan can reduce leadership risk and provide continuity for Harmony’s commercial and pipeline strategy. The reaffirmed 2026 WAKIX revenue guidance and expected Q4 2026 BP-205 data readout signal that the company does not anticipate near-term operational disruption from the transition. Anastasiou’s experience in capital raising and business development could be relevant as Harmony pursues its stated priorities of deploying capital strategically and transacting on value-creating assets.

However, the filing notes that the company’s business is subject to risks including the loss or retirement of key members of management, significant competition, the availability of favorable insurance coverage and reimbursement for WAKIX, and the timing and ability to obtain regulatory approvals for additional indications. These and other factors discussed under “Risk Factors” in the company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC on February 24, 2026, could cause actual results to differ materially.

## At a glance

 • WAKIX has achieved durable monopoly economics with Q2 2026 revenue of $261.3 million (+30% YoY) and full-year guidance of $1.0–1.04 billion, supported by IP exclusivity through March 2030 and settlements with six of seven generic filers, creating a self-funding engine that generated $348.2 million in annual operating cash flow. 

 • The pipeline transition is the central investment variable: BP-205, an orexin-2 receptor agonist with 600-fold selectivity and once-daily dosing potential, enters Phase 1b in Q3 2026 with data expected in early 2027, representing Harmony's bet to leapfrog current narcolepsy treatments and expand into broader CNS indications before WAKIX faces generic erosion. 

 • Concentration risk collides with capital allocation discipline: With 100% of revenue from WAKIX and $962.5 million in cash against $155 million in outstanding debt, Harmony faces the classic single-product biotech dilemma—whether to return capital or aggressively deploy it toward M&A to build a multi-franchise portfolio before its valuation multiple compresses. 

 • Competitive positioning is stronger than scale suggests: While Jazz Pharmaceuticals (JAZZ) dominates with a $2 billion+ rare sleep franchise, Harmony's focused execution has delivered 40% CAGR over five years and 75.4% gross margins, trading at 13.8x earnings versus Jazz's 16.2x, suggesting the market may underappreciate WAKIX's differentiation as the only non-scheduled narcolepsy treatment. 

 • Two binary outcomes define the risk/reward: Success in BP-205 Phase 2 trials (initiating mid-2027) and Pitolisant GR approval (PDUFA April 1, 2027) could transform Harmony into a multi-product CNS leader, while any delay or competitive orexin breakthrough from Takeda (TAK) would leave the company exposed as a single-product franchise with a finite 3.5-year exclusivity window.
